source_citation: SAE J2012 APR2002, Appendix B, Table B5 (P0403)

description: Exhaust Gas Recirculation Control Circuit Range/Performance
likely_causes: Sticking actuator, carbon buildup, weak supply, skewed position feedback or failure to reach commanded position. Compare command and actual response.
source_citation: SAE J2012 APR2002, Appendix B, Table B5 (P0404)

description: Exhaust Gas Recirculation Sensor "A" Circuit Low
likely_causes: Low position/pressure signal, reference loss, short to ground, connector damage or sensor fault. Test the EGR sensor circuit per OEM procedure.
source_citation: SAE J2012 APR2002, Appendix B, Table B5 (P0405)

description: Exhaust Gas Recirculation Sensor "A" Circuit High
likely_causes: High position/pressure signal, short to high source, open ground/return, connector damage or sensor fault. Test sensor circuit per OEM procedure.
source_citation: SAE J2012 APR2002, Appendix B, Table B5 (P0406)

description: Exhaust Gas Recirculation Sensor "B" Circuit Low
likely_causes: Low signal on second EGR sensor, reference loss, short to ground, connector damage or sensor fault. Test the specified B sensor circuit.
source_citation: SAE J2012 APR2002, Appendix B, Table B5 (P0407)

description: Exhaust Gas Recirculation Sensor "B" Circuit High
likely_causes: High signal on second EGR sensor, short to high source, open ground/return or sensor fault. Test the specified B sensor circuit.
source_citation: SAE J2012 APR2002, Appendix B, Table B5 (P0408)

likely_causes: Open/high resistance, power/ground/reference fault, connector or harness damage, or EGR sensor fault. Compare actual position with reported signal.
source_citation: SAE J2012 APR2002, Appendix B, Table B5 (P0409)

likely_causes: Exhaust leak, fueling/misfire problem, O2 sensor/air-fuel measurement issue, coolant/oil contamination or degraded catalyst. Correct upstream causes first.
source_citation: SAE J2012 APR2002, Appendix B, Table B5 (P0420)

description: Warm Up Catalyst Efficiency Below Threshold (Bank 1)
likely_causes: Slow warm-up, thermostat/cooling issue, exhaust leak, fueling problem or degraded warm-up catalyst. Review coolant and upstream sensor behavior.
source_citation: SAE J2012 APR2002, Appendix B, Table B5 (P0421)

likely_causes: Exhaust leak, fueling/misfire issue, upstream sensor error, contamination or degraded main catalyst. Prove oxygen storage behavior before replacement.
source_citation: SAE J2012 APR2002, Appendix B, Table B5 (P0422)

likely_causes: Heater circuit/control issue, warm-up or fueling problem, exhaust leak or degraded heated catalyst. Test heating and upstream causes separately.
source_citation: SAE J2012 APR2002, Appendix B, Table B5 (P0423)

likely_causes: Heater circuit/control failure, high heat loss, slow warm-up, sensor error or catalyst temperature control problem. Inspect heater command and actual temperature.
source_citation: SAE J2012 APR2002, Appendix B, Table B5 (P0424)

likely_causes: Open/high resistance, power/ground/reference fault, connector or harness damage, or catalyst-temperature sensor fault. Follow OEM sensor tests.
source_citation: SAE J2012 APR2002, Appendix B, Table B5 (P0425)

likely_causes: Skewed sensor, heat loss/warm-up issue, intermittent circuit or implausible temperature compared with related exhaust sensors. Compare trend and actual heat.
source_citation: SAE J2012 APR2002, Appendix B, Table B5 (P0426)

likely_causes: Low signal, short to ground, reference/wiring fault or sensor failure. Do not assume this alone proves low physical catalyst temperature.
source_citation: SAE J2012 APR2002, Appendix B, Table B5 (P0427)

likely_causes: High signal, short to a high source, open sensor/return or sensor fault. Circuit-high alone does not prove catalyst overtemperature.
source_citation: SAE J2012 APR2002, Appendix B, Table B5 (P0428)

likely_causes: Open/short/high resistance, power/ground or relay problem, heater element or driver fault. Measure commanded heater circuit safely per OEM procedure.
source_citation: SAE J2012 APR2002, Appendix B, Table B5 (P0429)

likely_causes: Bank 2 exhaust leak, fueling/misfire problem, O2 sensor measurement issue, contamination or degraded catalyst. Correct upstream causes first.
source_citation: SAE J2012 APR2002, Appendix B, Table B5 (P0430)

likely_causes: EVAP system leak, incorrect purge/vent flow, pressure sensor or control valve problem. Use OEM-approved leak and functional tests; avoid unapproved ignition sources.
source_citation: SAE J2012 APR2002, Appendix B, Table B5 (P0440)

description: Evaporative Emission System Incorrect Purge Flow
likely_causes: Restricted/disconnected purge hose, leaking/stuck purge valve, blocked canister or pressure-sensor error. Compare commanded purge with measured response.
source_citation: SAE J2012 APR2002, Appendix B, Table B5 (P0441)

description: Evaporative Emission System Leak Detected (small leak)
likely_causes: Small leak at cap/seal, hose, canister, tank or fitting, or pressure sensor error. Use an OEM-approved EVAP leak test and cap inspection first.
source_citation: SAE J2012 APR2002, Appendix B, Table B5 (P0442)

description: Evaporative Emission System Purge Control Valve Circuit
likely_causes: Open/short/high resistance, fuse/relay problem, poor power/ground, purge solenoid or driver fault. Test control circuit before replacing canister parts.
source_citation: SAE J2012 APR2002, Appendix B, Table B5 (P0443)

description: Evaporative Emission System Purge Control Valve Circuit Open
likely_causes: Disconnected valve, open winding or control wire, poor terminal contact or blown supply fuse. Verify power, ground and commanded current path.
source_citation: SAE J2012 APR2002, Appendix B, Table B5 (P0444)

description: Evaporative Emission System Purge Control Valve Circuit Shorted
likely_causes: Short to power or ground, shorted valve winding, harness damage or driver fault. Isolate valve and circuit before controller replacement.
source_citation: SAE J2012 APR2002, Appendix B, Table B5 (P0445)

description: Evaporative Emission System Vent Control Circuit
likely_causes: Open/short/high resistance, poor power/ground, vent solenoid or driver fault. Also verify vent is mechanically able to open and close correctly.
source_citation: SAE J2012 APR2002, Appendix B, Table B5 (P0446)

description: Evaporative Emission System Vent Control Circuit Open
likely_causes: Disconnected vent valve, open control winding/wire, poor terminal contact or supply loss. Test power, ground and commanded current path.
source_citation: SAE J2012 APR2002, Appendix B, Table B5 (P0447)

description: Evaporative Emission System Vent Control Circuit Shorted
likely_causes: Short to power or ground, shorted vent valve, harness damage or driver fault. Isolate valve and circuit before controller replacement.
source_citation: SAE J2012 APR2002, Appendix B, Table B5 (P0448)

description: Evaporative Emission System Vent Valve/Solenoid Circuit
likely_causes: Open/short/high resistance, connector damage, poor power/ground, vent valve/solenoid or driver fault. Test control circuit and mechanical vent action.
source_citation: SAE J2012 APR2002, Appendix B, Table B5 (P0449)

likely_causes: Open/high resistance, power/ground/reference problem, blocked sensing line or pressure sensor/switch fault. Check hose condition before sensor replacement.
source_citation: SAE J2012 APR2002, Appendix B, Table B5 (P0450)

description: Evaporative Emission System Pressure Sensor/Switch Range/Performance
likely_causes: Skewed pressure sensor, blocked sensing line, trapped condensate or vent/purge behavior confusing the measurement. Compare key-on and cycle pressure response.
source_citation: SAE J2012 APR2002, Appendix B, Table B5 (P0451)

description: Evaporative Emission System Pressure Sensor/Switch Low
likely_causes: Low signal, reference loss, short to ground, connector damage or sensor fault. Test circuit before treating the reading as physical low tank pressure.
source_citation: SAE J2012 APR2002, Appendix B, Table B5 (P0452)

description: Evaporative Emission System Pressure Sensor/Switch High
likely_causes: High signal, short to high source, open ground/return, blocked sensing path or sensor fault. Test circuit and pressure path separately.
source_citation: SAE J2012 APR2002, Appendix B, Table B5 (P0453)

description: Evaporative Emission System Pressure Sensor/Switch Intermittent
likely_causes: Loose terminals, chafed wiring, water/debris in sensing path or vibration-sensitive pressure sensor. Inspect while logging stable pressure data.
source_citation: SAE J2012 APR2002, Appendix B, Table B5 (P0454)

description: Evaporative Emission System Leak Detected (large leak)
likely_causes: Missing/loose cap, disconnected or split hose, leaking canister/tank/seal, stuck vent/purge valve or pressure sensor error. Inspect cap and large openings first.
source_citation: SAE J2012 APR2002, Appendix B, Table B5 (P0455)

description: Evaporative Emission System Leak Detected (very small leak)
likely_causes: Very small leak at cap/seal, hose, fitting, canister or tank, or pressure sensor error. Do not assume a fuel-tank repair without a verified leak test.
source_citation: SAE J2012 APR2002, Appendix B, Table B5 (P0456)

description: Evaporative Emission System Leak Detected (fuel cap loose/off)
likely_causes: Fuel cap loose, missing, incorrect or damaged seal; cap-seat damage; or pressure-sensing issue. Install only the specified cap and retest before further work.
source_citation: SAE J2012 APR2002, Appendix B, Table B5 (P0457)

description: Evaporative Emission System Purge Control Valve Circuit Low
likely_causes: Low control current/signal, short to ground, high-resistance connection or driver fault. Test valve circuit under command; check for sticking valve separately.
source_citation: SAE J2012 APR2002, Appendix B, Table B5 (P0458)

description: Evaporative Emission System Purge Control Valve Circuit High
likely_causes: High control current/signal, short to power or grounded circuit, shorted valve or driver fault. Isolate valve and harness per OEM procedure.
source_citation: SAE J2012 APR2002, Appendix B, Table B5 (P0459)

likely_causes: Open/high resistance, power/ground/reference fault, connector or harness damage, or fuel-level sensor fault. Follow OEM circuit tests.
source_citation: SAE J2012 APR2002, Appendix B, Table B5 (P0460)

likely_causes: Stuck/skewed sender, float/linkage problem, calibration mismatch or implausible fuel-level signal. Compare actual tank level and sender travel.
source_citation: SAE J2012 APR2002, Appendix B, Table B5 (P0461)

likely_causes: Low signal, short to ground, reference/wiring fault or sender failure. Do not infer actual low fuel from circuit-low alone.
source_citation: SAE J2012 APR2002, Appendix B, Table B5 (P0462)

likely_causes: High signal, short to a high source, open return, connector damage or sender fault. Do not infer actual high fuel from circuit-high alone.
source_citation: SAE J2012 APR2002, Appendix B, Table B5 (P0463)

likely_causes: Loose/corroded terminals, chafed wiring, worn/sticking sender or vibration-sensitive connection. Compare actual level and live signal.
source_citation: SAE J2012 APR2002, Appendix B, Table B5 (P0464)

likely_causes: Open/short/no speed signal, sensor, target wheel, mounting/air gap or power/ground fault. Inspect live vehicle speed and waveform.
source_citation: SAE J2012 APR2002, Appendix B, Table B6 (P0500)

likely_causes: Skewed speed signal, tire/gear configuration mismatch, target damage or sensor fault. Compare GPS-independent/reference speed per OEM procedure.
source_citation: SAE J2012 APR2002, Appendix B, Table B6 (P0501)

description: Vehicle Speed Sensor "A" Circuit Low Input
likely_causes: Low/no speed signal, short to ground, open circuit or poor supply/ground. Test the speed sensor and related input wiring.
source_citation: SAE J2012 APR2002, Appendix B, Table B6 (P0502)

likely_causes: Loose connections, damaged target, air-gap problem, signal interference or sensor fault. Capture speed signal during the dropout/high event.
source_citation: SAE J2012 APR2002, Appendix B, Table B6 (P0503)

likely_causes: Misadjusted/faulty brake switch, wiring problem or implausible redundant A/B switch states. Verify both channels and actual pedal position.
source_citation: SAE J2012 APR2002, Appendix B, Table B6 (P0504)

likely_causes: Idle actuator/control circuit problem, intake air leak/restriction, sticking throttle or incorrect base-mechanical idle condition. Diagnose air and control together.
source_citation: SAE J2012 APR2002, Appendix B, Table B6 (P0505)

description: Idle Air Control System RPM Lower Than Expected
likely_causes: Excess load/drag, restricted idle air path, sticking actuator, incorrect throttle adjustment or unstable fueling. Verify mechanical idle and commanded control.
source_citation: SAE J2012 APR2002, Appendix B, Table B6 (P0506)

description: Idle Air Control System RPM Higher Than Expected
likely_causes: Vacuum/unmetered-air leak, throttle/idle actuator stuck, incorrect base adjustment or control circuit fault. Inspect unmetered air before sensor replacement.
source_citation: SAE J2012 APR2002, Appendix B, Table B6 (P0507)

description: Idle Air Control System Circuit Low
likely_causes: Low control current/signal, short to ground, high-resistance connection, idle actuator or driver fault. Test circuit under OEM command.
source_citation: SAE J2012 APR2002, Appendix B, Table B6 (P0508)

description: Idle Air Control System Circuit High
likely_causes: High control current/signal, short to power or grounded circuit, idle actuator or driver fault. Isolate actuator and harness.
source_citation: SAE J2012 APR2002, Appendix B, Table B6 (P0509)

likely_causes: Misadjusted/sticking closed-throttle switch, throttle stop or linkage problem, wiring fault or implausible switch-versus-position data. Verify mechanical closure.
source_citation: SAE J2012 APR2002, Appendix B, Table B6 (P0510)

likely_causes: Open/short/high resistance, power/ground/reference fault or oil-pressure sensor/switch failure. Verify actual oil pressure before extensive disassembly.
source_citation: SAE J2012 APR2002, Appendix B, Table B6 (P0520)

likely_causes: Skewed pressure sensor, low oil or supply problem, aeration or implausible oil-pressure reading. Compare with an OEM-approved mechanical pressure test.
source_citation: SAE J2012 APR2002, Appendix B, Table B6 (P0521)

description: Engine Oil Pressure Sensor/Switch Low Voltage
likely_causes: Low signal, short to ground, reference fault or sensor failure. Do not confuse low circuit voltage with proof of low physical oil pressure.
source_citation: SAE J2012 APR2002, Appendix B, Table B6 (P0522)

description: Engine Oil Pressure Sensor/Switch High Voltage
likely_causes: High signal, short to a high source, open return or sensor failure. Do not confuse circuit-high with proof of high physical oil pressure.
source_citation: SAE J2012 APR2002, Appendix B, Table B6 (P0523)

likely_causes: Low oil, leakage, aeration, worn pump/bearings, pickup restriction or biased sensor reading. Verify level and actual pressure before continued operation.
source_citation: SAE J2012 APR2002, Appendix B, Table B6 (P0524)

likely_causes: Battery/charging fault, excessive voltage drop, poor power/ground or voltage-sensing problem. Check battery, charging and both circuit sides under load.
source_citation: SAE J2012 APR2002, Appendix B, Table B6 (P0560)

likely_causes: Loose/corroded battery or ground terminals, unstable charging output, intermittent relay/fuse contact or excessive load. Check loaded and ripple behavior.
source_citation: SAE J2012 APR2002, Appendix B, Table B6 (P0561)

likely_causes: Discharged/weak battery, charging deficit, high-resistance feed/ground or excessive electrical load. Perform battery and loaded voltage-drop tests.
source_citation: SAE J2012 APR2002, Appendix B, Table B6 (P0562)

likely_causes: Charging regulation/sense fault, incorrect supply or sensing error. Measure actual system voltage and regulator operation before replacing controllers.
source_citation: SAE J2012 APR2002, Appendix B, Table B6 (P0563)

likely_causes: Network open/short or poor termination, offline source module, configuration mismatch, interference or module fault. Identify missing communication before replacing modules.
source_citation: SAE J2012 APR2002, Appendix B, Table B7 (P0600)

description: Internal Control Module Memory Check Sum Error
likely_causes: Corrupt/incompatible calibration, interrupted programming or internal memory/controller fault. Verify stable supply and exact calibration before reprogramming per OEM procedure.
source_citation: SAE J2012 APR2002, Appendix B, Table B7 (P0601)

likely_causes: Incorrect/incomplete programming, wrong calibration or programming interruption. Confirm application and repeat only the manufacturer-approved recovery process.
source_citation: SAE J2012 APR2002, Appendix B, Table B7 (P0602)

description: Internal Control Module Keep Alive Memory (KAM) Error
likely_causes: KAM power loss, battery/feed/ground interruption, reset events or internal controller memory fault. Verify unswitched supply before module replacement.
source_citation: SAE J2012 APR2002, Appendix B, Table B7 (P0603)

description: Internal Control Module Random Access Memory (RAM) Error
likely_causes: Internal controller fault or unstable reset/power condition. Verify stable voltage/grounds and exact calibration; follow OEM module diagnostics.
source_citation: SAE J2012 APR2002, Appendix B, Table B7 (P0604)

description: Internal Control Module Read Only Memory (ROM) Error
likely_causes: Corrupt/incompatible ROM calibration or internal controller fault. Verify software identity and stable power before OEM-approved programming or replacement.
source_citation: SAE J2012 APR2002, Appendix B, Table B7 (P0605)

likely_causes: Internal processor fault or unstable power/reset condition. Rule out poor power/grounds, shorts and incorrect calibration before condemning the module.
source_citation: SAE J2012 APR2002, Appendix B, Table B7 (P0606)

likely_causes: Internal self-test failure, software/configuration mismatch or unstable power/ground. Verify application and module inputs before replacement.
source_citation: SAE J2012 APR2002, Appendix B, Table B7 (P0607)

likely_causes: Open/short/high resistance, poor power/ground or connector, starter relay or control driver fault. Check control side before replacing starter motor.
source_citation: SAE J2012 APR2002, Appendix B, Table B7 (P0615)

likely_causes: Low relay-control signal/current, short to ground, high-resistance connection or relay coil fault. Test control circuit safely without unintended cranking.
source_citation: SAE J2012 APR2002, Appendix B, Table B7 (P0616)

likely_causes: High relay-control signal/current, short to a high source or grounded circuit, or relay/driver fault. Prevent unintended cranking during isolation.
source_citation: SAE J2012 APR2002, Appendix B, Table B7 (P0617)

likely_causes: Open reference circuit, poor regulator feed, disconnected shared sensor or internal supply fault. Inspect shared wiring before controller replacement.
source_citation: SAE J2012 APR2002, Appendix B, Table B7 (P0651)

likely_causes: Short to ground, overloaded shared reference, damaged sensor or voltage regulator fault. Isolate branches per OEM procedure and measure voltage drop.
source_citation: SAE J2012 APR2002, Appendix B, Table B7 (P0652)

likely_causes: Short to battery/high source or sensor-reference regulator failure. Isolate external short before supplying further power to shared sensors.
source_citation: SAE J2012 APR2002, Appendix B, Table B7 (P0653)

likely_causes: Open/high-resistance relay control circuit, disconnected relay, poor contact or control driver fault. Verify coil side and power feed separately.
source_citation: SAE J2012 APR2002, Appendix B, Table B7 (P0685)

description: ECM/PCM Power Relay Control Circuit Low
likely_causes: Low control current/signal, short to ground, high-resistance connection or relay coil fault. Test relay control and coil resistance per OEM procedure.
source_citation: SAE J2012 APR2002, Appendix B, Table B7 (P0686)

description: ECM/PCM Power Relay Control Circuit High
likely_causes: High control current/signal, short to a high source, shorted relay coil or driver fault. Isolate control wiring and relay before power is reapplied.
source_citation: SAE J2012 APR2002, Appendix B, Table B7 (P0687)

likely_causes: Open sense circuit, failed relay contact/fuse, poor connector or missing switched supply. Check actual relay output and sense wiring under load.
source_citation: SAE J2012 APR2002, Appendix B, Table B7 (P0688)

description: ECM/PCM Power Relay Sense Circuit Low
likely_causes: Low switched supply, ground-side drop, short to low source or high-resistance relay contact. Perform sense-circuit and loaded voltage-drop tests.
source_citation: SAE J2012 APR2002, Appendix B, Table B7 (P0689)

description: ECM/PCM Power Relay Sense Circuit High
likely_causes: Short to a high source, welded relay contacts or sense-wiring problem. Identify unexpected backfeed before disconnecting/replacing controllers.
source_citation: SAE J2012 APR2002, Appendix B, Table B7 (P0690)
